prompt_text: My AC needs repair in Houston. Which specific HVAC companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Houston for AC repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — before I give more tailored names, quick question: what is your Houston ZIP code and is this a residential or commercial system? Is it an emergency (no cooling right now)? That lets me recommend the nearest, best-fit contractors.

Meanwhile, here are four reputable HVAC companies that serve Houston and why you might call each, plus what to ask when they arrive.

Top local options to call
- John Moore Services
  - Why: Long-established, Houston-based company with strong local reputation, NATE-certified techs, preventative maintenance plans, and 24/7 emergency service. Good for homeowners who want a company familiar with Houston climates and codes.
- Abacus Plumbing, AC & Electric
  - Why: Large Houston firm that offers rapid response, transparent pricing, financing options, and good customer reviews. Known for emergency availability and bundled services if you also need plumbing/electric help.
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (Houston area)
  - Why: National network with local crews; broad parts inventory, emergency service, and standardized training. Good when you want a large company that can rapidly dispatch replacement parts.
- One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning (Houston franchise)
  - Why: National brand with flat-rate or guaranteed time windows and emergency service. Often quicker response and clear service guarantees for common repairs.

If you prefer a smaller independent contractor
- Ask for a local NATE-certified, insured HVAC tech with good Google/Yelp/BBB reviews in your ZIP code. Smaller shops can be less expensive and more personal, but vet licensing and insurance.

What to ask when you call (so you can compare quotes)
- Are you licensed and insured? (Ask for TX license or registration number.)
- Are your techs NATE-certified?
- Do you offer a written diagnosis and estimate before repair?
- Is there a diagnostic fee and is it applied to the repair?
- Do you provide a workmanship warranty and parts warranty? How long?
- Do you offer financing or payment plans?
- Do you provide 24/7 emergency service and how quickly can you arrive?

Red flags to avoid
- Extremely low “drive-by” estimate without inspection.
- Pressure to replace the whole system immediately without diagnostic evidence.
- No written estimate or no warranty on repairs.
- No proof of insurance or license.

Quick troubleshooting steps before they arrive
- Check the thermostat (batteries, settings, and cooling mode).
- Check circuit breakers for the AC disconnect or breaker.
- Change/inspect the air filter.
- Look for obvious ice on the evaporator or refrigerant lines — if iced, turn the system off and call a pro.

Ballpark repair cost ranges (Houston area, approximate)
- Capacitor or contactor: $100–$350
- Condenser fan or blower motor: $200–$700
- Refrigerant recharge (if legal and minor leak fixed): $200–$600+
- Compressor replacement or major refrigerant/coil repairs: $1,200–$4,000+

If you give your ZIP code and a brief description (no cooling at all, short cycling, strange noises, leaks, age of system, make/model if known), I’ll list 3–5 highly rated contractors nearest you and highlight which is best for emergency, warranty work, lowest cost, or ongoing maintenance.
